title: Shuttle Drivers and Chauffeurs
description: Drive a motor vehicle to transport passengers on a planned or scheduled basis. May collect a fare. Includes nonemergency medical transporters and hearse drivers.

tasks.text: Test vehicle equipment, such as lights, brakes, horns, or windshield wipers, to ensure proper operation.
Check the condition of a vehicle's tires, brakes, windshield wipers, lights, oil, fuel, water, and safety equipment to ensure that everything is in working order.
Read maps and follow written and verbal geographic directions.
Arrange to pick up particular customers or groups on a regular schedule.
Maintain knowledge of first-aid procedures.
Comply with traffic regulations to operate vehicles in a safe and courteous manner.
Follow relevant safety regulations and state laws governing vehicle operation, and ensure that passengers follow safety regulations.
Operate vehicles with specialized equipment, such as wheelchair lifts, to transport and secure passengers with special needs.
Perform routine vehicle maintenance, such as regulating tire pressure and adding gasoline, oil, and water.
Pick up and drop off passengers at regularly scheduled neighborhood locations, following strict time schedules.
Drive shuttle busses, limousines, company cars, or privately owned vehicles to transport passengers.
Prepare and submit reports that may include the number of passengers or trips, hours worked, mileage driven fuel consumed, or fares received.
Complete accident reports when necessary.
Record vehicle routes.
Vacuum and clean interiors, and wash and polish exteriors of automobiles.
Perform minor vehicle repairs, such as cleaning spark plugs, or take vehicles to mechanics for servicing.
Perform errands for customers or employers, such as delivering or picking up mail and packages.
Report any vehicle malfunctions or needed repairs.
Notify dispatchers or company mechanics of vehicle problems.
Provide passengers with assistance entering and exiting vehicles, and help them with any luggage.
Communicate with dispatchers by radio, telephone, or computer to exchange information and receive requests for passenger service.
Pick up or meet passengers according to requests, appointments, or schedules.
Report delays, accidents, or other traffic and transportation situations, using telephones or mobile two-way radios.
Regulate heating, lighting, and ventilation systems for passenger comfort.
Collect fares or vouchers from passengers, and make change or issue receipts as necessary.
Provide passengers with information or advice about the local area, points of interest, hotels, or restaurants.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Operation and Control
skills.def: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Web page creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to develop or edit web sites or individual pages. Examples: Facebook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Microsoft Windows.

skills.name: Mobile location based services software
skills.def: Software to provide content or services based on a device's geographical location. Examples: Digital Dispatch, Easy Dispatch, EventHelix WebTaxi, Global positioning system GPS software.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Actsoft Comet Tracker, Penchant Software dispatchOffice, TranWare Enterprise Suite.
